findings.claim: The new boundary test exercises only the `isInstalledDependencyResolution` predicate on string inputs, not `resolveLocalRuntimeImport`'s new early return, so the integration point the CI failure lived in is covered only indirectly by the pinned 186-path closure assertion.
findings.reproduction: Read tests/promptRefinerRuntimeSourceClosure.test.mjs:1150-1154: the three assertions call the predicate directly and never call resolveLocalRuntimeImport. Delete line 224 (`if (isInstalledDependencyResolution(path)) return null;`) and run `node --import tsx --test tests/promptRefinerRuntimeSourceClosure.test.mjs`: the test at line 1150 still passes; only the closure test at line 1022 reports the change. An added `assert.equal(resolveLocalRuntimeImport("lib/promptRefinerStageAdmission.ts", "typescript"), null)` would pin the early return itself (note it is only discriminating on a checkout whose node_modules is inside the repository, i.e. the Linux layout).

findings.claim: The early return is placed before the `local workspace import resolved outside repository` assertion at line 234, so a `@tomverse/*` import that ever resolved to a real (non-symlinked) copy under node_modules would be silently classified external instead of failing on that guard.
findings.reproduction: Read lines 217-240: the `isInstalledDependencyResolution` return at 224 precedes both the `.d.ts` assertion (227) and the workspace assertion (234). The behaviour is still fail-closed — the closure would then omit packages/chat-core/src/index.ts and `assert.deepEqual([...PROMPT_REFINER_RUNTIME_SOURCE_PATHS], expected)` at line 1036 fails — but the message names a path list rather than the workspace rule. Gating the early return on `workspace === null` would keep the precise message; today's workspace layout (npm symlink, realpath into packages/*) is unaffected either way, which line 1158 confirms.

findings.claim: A third PostgreSQL suite truncates the same three tables but still with `CASCADE`, so the no-CASCADE cleanup rule this change establishes is not uniform across the FK's dependents (pre-existing from PR #1555 and outside this task's writable scope, so not actionable here).
findings.reproduction: `rg -U 'TRUNCATE TABLE[^;]*"AdminAuditLog"[^;]*RESTART IDENTITY( CASCADE)?' tests/integration` shows prompt-refiner-reservation-admission.db.test.ts:56-57 ending in `RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE`, while the two suites changed here end in `RESTART IDENTITY`. That suite runs in the `finance` lane (scripts/db-integration-groups.mjs:73 matches `prompt-refiner-reservation`), so it is not covered by the accounts lane the author ran.

verdict.nextAction: Merge as CI consistency: the two accounts-lane cleanups name all three FK-linked tables in one statement without CASCADE and every other AdminAuditLog truncation in the repository already uses CASCADE; the 20260918130000 migration and lib/promptRefinerStageAdmission.ts allowlist entries match the file contents (2 AdminAuditLog mentions, FK plus read-only trigger SELECT, one constant `LOCK TABLE "ModelRegistryEntry"` via $executeRawUnsafe) and permit no protected-table write; lib/promptRefinerStageAdmissionCore.ts names providerFallbackCandidates only as a path literal in PROMPT_REFINER_RUNTIME_SOURCE_PATHS, importing no export and dispatching nothing — the three nits above are recorded and need no revision round, and note that the PostgreSQL accounts lane result is the author's claim, not something this read-only review re-ran.
